answer:
Using \(L=10\log_{10}(I/I_0)\):

- Source 1: \(L_1=60\ \text{dB}\Rightarrow I_1/I_0=10^{60/10}=10^6\)
- Source 2: \(L_2=66\ \text{dB}\Rightarrow I_2/I_0=10^{66/10}=10^{6.6}\)

### 1. Both sources running continuously
Independent sound intensities add:

\[
L_{\text{both}}=10\log_{10}\left(10^{60/10}+10^{66/10}\right)
\]

\[
L_{\text{both}}=10\log_{10}\left(10^6+10^{6.6}\right)\approx 66.97\ \text{dB}
\]

So the combined level is approximately:

\[
\boxed{67.0\ \text{dB}}
\]

### 2. Only one runs at a time for equal durations
The equivalent continuous level uses average intensity:

\[
L_{\text{eq}}=10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I_1+I_2}{2I_0}\right)
\]

\[
L_{\text{eq}}=10\log_{10}\left(\frac{10^6+10^{6.6}}{2}\right)
\approx 63.96\ \text{dB}
\]

So:

\[
\boxed{L_{\text{eq}}\approx 63.96\ \text{dB}\approx 64.0\ \text{dB}}
\]

### 3. Arithmetic mean of the two dB readings

\[
\frac{60+66}{2}=63\ \text{dB}
\]

Thus:

\[
\boxed{\text{Arithmetic mean}=63.0\ \text{dB}}
\]

### Comparison
- Both sources continuously: \(\boxed{66.97\ \text{dB}\approx 67.0\ \text{dB}}\)
- Equal-time alternating equivalent level: \(\boxed{63.96\ \text{dB}\approx 64.0\ \text{dB}}\)
- Arithmetic mean of dB values: \(\boxed{63.0\ \text{dB}}\)

The arithmetic mean of decibel readings is not the correct energy average. For equal-duration alternating operation, it underestimates the equivalent level by about:

\[
63.96-63.0 \approx \boxed{0.96\ \text{dB}}
\]

So the equivalent constant level is about \(\boxed{64.0\ \text{dB}}\), not simply \(\boxed{63.0\ \text{dB}}\).
